system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Friedreich ataxia due to FXN deficiency
mechanism: Most Friedreich ataxia results from biallelic intronic GAA-repeat expansions that reduce FXN transcription and frataxin. Frataxin deficiency impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, disrupts respiratory-chain and aconitase function, mislocalizes iron, and increases oxidative stress.
vignette: An adolescent develops progressive gait ataxia, dysarthria, loss of vibration and position sense, absent lower-extremity reflexes, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Genetic testing shows biallelic GAA-repeat expansions in FXN.
lead: Which of the following cellular abnormalities most directly results from this mutation?
correct: Defective mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis due to reduced frataxin expression
distractors: Failure of lysosomal GM2 degradation due to hexosaminidase A deficiency
Defective peroxisomal import of very-long-chain fatty-acid oxidation enzymes
Impaired myelin compaction due to duplication of the PMP22 gene
Defective copper incorporation into cytochrome c oxidase due to ATP7A deficiency
distractor_notes: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease and does not explain the FXN GAA-repeat expansion or cardiomyopathy-associated ataxia.
Peroxisomal protein-import defects cause Zellweger-spectrum disease, not Friedreich ataxia.
PMP22 duplication causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A, a peripheral neuropathy without the characteristic FXN/frataxin mitochondrial mechanism.
ATP7A deficiency causes Menkes disease through impaired copper transport, not frataxin-dependent iron-sulfur cluster failure.
key_expl: Frataxin is a mitochondrial iron-binding protein required for iron-sulfur cluster assembly. GAA-repeat expansions in FXN suppress frataxin expression. The downstream result is deficiency of iron-sulfur-cluster enzymes, mitochondrial iron mislocalization, impaired respiratory function, and oxidative stress, producing the neurologic and cardiac manifestations of Friedreich ataxia.
objective: Connect FXN GAA-repeat expansion in Friedreich ataxia with reduced frataxin and impaired mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis.
